AI.conclusion: Quasi-steady coronal heating scales with magnetic flux, while rho_tot may specifically contribute to high-temperature coronal heating. At lower temperatures, regions storing more energy than expected for their flux produce less EUV emission than expected, indicating that flux remains the dominant driver of coronal emission.

title: Simulating Ionospheric Distortions in Mock SKA-Low Solar Radio Observations
summary: The Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) will provide unprecedented angular resolution for low-frequency solar radio imaging, enabling access to fine-scale coronal structures. However, the improved spatial resolution of SKA-Low also increases the sensitivity of solar images to ionospheric propagation effects. We investigate the impact of ionospheric fluctuations on simulated SKA-Low solar observations at 50, 100, 150, and 200 MHz using the \textsc{Karabo} simulator and turbulent, moving ionospheric phase screens. We quantify the resulting image distortions using spatial power spectral density (PSD) analysis and compare the SKA response with corresponding MWA simulations. The results show that ionospheric distortions are strongly scale- and frequency-dependent, with the maximum fractional PSD distortion decreasing with observing frequencies. SKA resolves ionospheric fluctuations over spatial scales that are largely smoothed by the MWA instrumental response, with significant distortions occurring on scales comparable to solar active-region structures. These results demonstrate that ionospheric propagation effects should be considered when interpreting high-resolution SKA-low solar radio images, particularly at the lower end of the frequency band.

AI.tldr: This study simulates ionospheric impacts on SKA-Low solar radio imaging at 50–200 MHz, showing that distortions are scale- and frequency-dependent and more pronounced at lower frequencies than for the MWA.
AI.motivation: SKAO's improved angular resolution enables fine-scale coronal imaging but also makes solar images more sensitive to ionospheric propagation effects, which must be characterized before interpreting high-resolution observations.
AI.method: The Karabo simulator was used with turbulent, moving ionospheric phase screens to simulate SKA-Low solar observations at 50, 100, 150, and 200 MHz. Image distortions were quantified via spatial power spectral density (PSD) analysis and compared with corresponding MWA simulations.
AI.result: Ionospheric distortions are strongly scale- and frequency-dependent, with maximum fractional PSD distortion decreasing as observing frequency increases. SKA resolves ionospheric fluctuations on spatial scales largely smoothed by the MWA instrumental response, with significant distortions at scales comparable to solar active-region structures.
AI.conclusion: Ionospheric propagation effects must be accounted for when interpreting high-resolution SKA-Low solar radio images, particularly at the lower end of the frequency band.

title: Dynamical and thermal evolution of localized reconnecting current sheets under varying guide-fields in the solar corona
comment: 19 pages, 15 figures, Accepted for publication in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: Although magnetic reconnection in coronal current sheets (CSs) is a fundamental energy release mechanism in the solar corona, the role of guide-fields in governing its formation and self-consistent evolution is not fully understood. Through 2.5D resistive magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations, we investigate how guide-fields affect the formation and evolution of a localized reconnecting coronal CS. Strong guide-fields prevent oppositely directed field lines from approaching sufficiently to form a CS, delaying and suppressing its subsequent evolution. The reconnection rate exhibits a rising phase resembling a power-law, with exponent $δ_1$ decreasing with rising guide-fields, indicating slower temporal growth of the reconnection rate. The aspect ratio of the CS follows a similar power-law trend with the exponent $α_1$ decreasing with rising guide-fields. A subsequent slower growth phase of the reconnection rate shows a power-law exponent $δ_2$ that increases with rising guide-fields, as does the corresponding aspect-ratio exponent $α_2$. As the CS evolves, the latter phase is achieved due to a sharp decremental transition of the guide-field within the CS after a time when the increasing inflows are inefficiently resisted by the guide-field itself. In the reconnection regime during prior phases, the power-law exponents of the maximum temperature and the outflow velocities also decrease with rising guide-fields demonstrating that stronger guide-fields suppress the growth of these indicators also. This study suggests that a self-consistently formed CS displays phases of efficient and inefficient quenching of the reconnection mechanism, promoted by non-zero guide-fields. We also quantify this behavior for indicators of the reconnection process and discuss their applicability to observations of apparent CSs and probing background coronal conditions.

AI.tldr: 2.5D resistive MHD simulations show that strong guide-fields delay coronal current sheet formation and suppress reconnection, producing two power-law phases whose exponents vary oppositely with guide-field strength.
AI.motivation: Magnetic reconnection in coronal current sheets (CSs) is a fundamental energy release mechanism in the solar corona, yet the role of guide-fields in governing CS formation and self-consistent evolution remains incompletely understood.
AI.method: 2.5D resistive magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of a localized reconnecting coronal current sheet, tracking the reconnection rate, CS aspect ratio, maximum temperature, and outflow velocities as functions of guide-field strength, with power-law fits to the temporal evolution.
AI.result: Strong guide-fields prevent oppositely directed field lines from approaching closely enough to form a CS, delaying and suppressing its evolution. The reconnection rate shows a rising power-law phase with exponent δ1 decreasing as guide-field rises (slower growth); the CS aspect ratio follows a similar trend with exponent α1 also decreasing. A later, slower growth phase has exponents δ2 and α2 that increase with guide-field strength. This latter phase arises from a sharp decremental transition of the guide-field inside the CS once increasing inflows are inefficiently resisted by the guide-field. During earlier reconnection phases, power-law exponents of maximum temperature and outflow velocities also decrease with rising guide-field, indicating suppression of these indicators.
AI.conclusion: A self-consistently formed CS exhibits phases of efficient and inefficient quenching of reconnection, promoted by non-zero guide-fields. The quantified behavior of reconnection indicators is discussed for applicability to observations of apparent CSs and for probing background coronal conditions.

title: MATISSE unveils a dusty disc in the interior of EP Aquarii. First evidence of a misaligned hierarchical triple system with a central AGB star?
comment: 10 pages, 12 figures and 3 tables
summary: Aims. We have mapped the dust and molecular gas emission distributions in the vicinity (a few stellar radii) of the asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star EP\,Aquarii, with a previously reported stellar companion at $\sim$50\,au, to search for binary-induced asymmetries. Methods. We present an analysis of new high-angular-resolution ($\gtrsim$4\,mas) images obtained with MATISSE (in the wavelength range $\sim$3--8\,\mum) as well as archival high-angular-resolution ($\gtrsim$20\,mas) ALMA $\rm^{12}$CO\,(c$J$=2-1) line and continuum emission observations ($\sim$230\,GHz), to study the circumstellar morphology and kinematics of the molecular gas on these spatial scales. Results. The MATISSE images display a bright central source and two slightly extended emission features ("blobs") located on opposite sides of the AGB star (at radial distances of $\sim$4--10\,au). These structures are consistent with previous mid-infrared interferometric observations, suggesting stability over decades. The central source is elongated along the direction defined by the blobs, in both the MATISSE and ALMA continuum images. The ALMA $\rm^{12}$CO\,($J$=2-1) maps display an asymmetric inner wind with a velocity gradient. Conclusions. The observations are consistent with an edge-on dusty equatorial overdensity (disc-like), hinting the presence of a close ($\lesssim$4\,au) companion. The inferred symmetry axis is almost perpendicular to the CO velocity gradient and the orbital plane proposed for the distant ($\sim$50\,au) companion. EP\,Aqr may represent the first misaligned hierarchical triple system with a central AGB star.

AI.tldr: High-resolution MATISSE and ALMA observations of EP Aquarii reveal an edge-on dusty equatorial overdensity with blobs and asymmetric CO wind, suggesting a close companion and a misaligned hierarchical triple system.
AI.motivation: To search for binary-induced asymmetries in the dust and molecular gas distribution near the AGB star EP Aquarii, which has a known stellar companion at ~50 au.
AI.method: Analysis of new high-angular-resolution (≳4 mas) MATISSE images (~3–8 µm) and archival high-angular-resolution (≳20 mas) ALMA 12CO(J=2-1) line and continuum observations (~230 GHz) to study circumstellar morphology and kinematics.
AI.result: MATISSE images show a bright central source and two slightly extended emission blobs on opposite sides at ~4–10 au, consistent with previous mid-infrared interferometry, indicating decade-scale stability. The central source is elongated along the blob axis in both MATISSE and ALMA continuum. ALMA 12CO maps reveal an asymmetric inner wind with a velocity gradient.
AI.conclusion: Observations are consistent with an edge-on dusty equatorial overdensity (disc-like), hinting at a close (≲4 au) companion. The inferred symmetry axis is nearly perpendicular to the CO velocity gradient and the orbital plane of the distant (~50 au) companion, making EP Aqr a possible first misaligned hierarchical triple system with a central AGB star.

title: The EBLM Project - XIX. The absence of radius inflation in a homogeneous analysis of 66 Northern low-mass eclipsing binaries
comment: 37 pages, 19 figures, 10 tables, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: Precise and accurate measurements of host stars are crucial in the search for Earth-like exoplanets, and M-dwarfs are favourable targets in this quest. Low-mass eclipsing binaries offer unique opportunities to empirically determine stellar masses and radii for low-mass stars where stellar models may be systematically biased. We present results from the EBLM-North sample, the largest homogeneous study of low-mass eclipsing binaries with secondary characterisation yet, combining high-resolution and high-precision radial velocities from SOPHIE and TESS photometry. We measure a median precision for stellar companions of 4.2% in radius and 8.6% in mass within a sub-sample of 50 high-quality binaries, all with orbital periods $P_{\rm bin} > 5\,\rm days$. We compare our data to the Baraffe and MIST isochrones, and find our sample is statistically consistent with those models, producing reduced chi-squared values, $χ^2_ν\sim 1$. Our measured radius inflation is $0.3\pm 1.6$% indicating no statistically significant trend. We likewise detect no significant trend with metallicity, despite having the precision to identify such a relationship. As such, our observations do not appear to follow the general metallicity trend predicted in MIST. A $χ_ν^2 \sim 1$ indicates the scatter in our results is commensurate with our uncertainties alone. These results constrain the scope for unmodelled effects on the mass-radius relation that would produce radius deviations greater than 4.2%. However, our secondary effective temperatures do not reproduce this high level of agreement with the models, and we do not recover the predicted trends with metallicity.

AI.tldr: The EBLM-North study characterizes 50 low-mass eclipsing binaries, measuring stellar companion radii and masses to median precisions of 4.2% and 8.6%, finding consistency with Baraffe and MIST isochrones and no significant radius inflation.
AI.motivation: Precise host-star measurements are essential for finding Earth-like exoplanets, and M-dwarfs are prime targets. Low-mass eclipsing binaries allow empirical determination of stellar masses and radii in a regime where stellar models may be systematically biased.
AI.method: The authors combine high-resolution, high-precision radial velocities from SOPHIE with TESS photometry to characterize the EBLM-North sample, a sub-sample of 50 high-quality binaries with orbital periods P_bin > 5 days. They compare results to Baraffe and MIST isochrones and examine radius inflation trends with metallicity.
AI.result: Median precision is 4.2% in radius and 8.6% in mass. The sample is statistically consistent with Baraffe and MIST isochrones (reduced chi-squared ~1). Measured radius inflation is 0.3 ± 1.6%, with no statistically significant trend. No significant metallicity trend is detected despite sufficient precision. However, secondary effective temperatures do not reproduce this high level of agreement, and predicted metallicity trends are not recovered.
AI.conclusion: The observations constrain unmodelled effects on the mass-radius relation to deviations greater than 4.2%, as scatter is commensurate with uncertainties alone. Radius and mass agree well with models, but effective temperatures and metallicity trends remain discrepant.

title: The EBLM project - XX. Absolute dynamical masses of five low-mass eclipsing binaries, and an evaluation of mass estimation methods
comment: 34 pages, 26 figures, 9 tables. Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: Eclipsing binaries consisting of a solar-type primary and an M dwarf secondary are key laboratories to study objects at the bottom of the main sequence. Fundamental parameters of such stars have a direct impact upon exoplanetary studies, as searches for temperate Earth-sized planets focus on M dwarf hosts. Eclipsing binaries are essential to measure these parameters. However for stellar masses $<$ 0.35 M$_\odot$ , few double-lined eclipsing systems are known. Thus, stellar evolution models and empirical relations have had to rely on single-lined eclipsing binaries, for instance those from the EBLM project (Eclipsing Binary - Low Mass). Using high resolution spectroscopy to extract the weak signal of the secondary (flux ratio $<$ 1 per cent in the optical), we transform five more systems from single to double-lined, deriving absolute masses for both stars. We then compare methods typically employed to estimate stellar masses for field stars or single-lined binaries with the absolute dynamical masses we obtain, to assess their accuracy. Our results for SB1 and SB2 analyses are mostly consistent within 1-$σ$, though we identify a small systematic overestimation of SB1 masses derived from a combination of radial velocities and eclipse photometry. We show that the bias originates from primary radius overestimation during isochronal analysis, wherein the secondary light reduces photometric magnitudes and impacts the recovered radii by modifying the spectral energy distribution. With proper calibration, we can ensure the accuracy of using the full EBLM SB1 sample to constrain mass-radius-luminosity relationships for the smallest, yet most abundant, stars in the Galaxy

Comparing these with SB1-derived masses reveals a small systematic overestimation caused by primary radius overestimation in isochronal analysis, which can be calibrated to validate the full EBLM SB1 sample.
AI.motivation: Eclipsing binaries with a solar-type primary and M dwarf secondary are key laboratories for studying the bottom of the main sequence and directly impact exoplanetary studies, since temperate Earth-sized planet searches target M dwarf hosts. However, for stellar masses below 0.35 M_sun, few double-lined eclipsing systems are known, forcing stellar evolution models and empirical relations to rely on single-lined eclipsing binaries such as those from the EBLM project.
AI.method: High-resolution spectroscopy was used to extract the weak signal of the secondary (flux ratio less than 1 percent in the optical), converting five more systems from single- to double-lined and deriving absolute masses for both stars. The dynamically obtained masses were then compared with methods typically employed to estimate stellar masses for field stars or single-lined binaries to assess their accuracy.

This bias originates from primary radius overestimation during isochronal analysis, where the secondary's light reduces photometric magnitudes and impacts the recovered radii by modifying the spectral energy distribution.
AI.conclusion: With proper calibration, the accuracy of using the full EBLM SB1 sample can be ensured to constrain mass-radius-luminosity relationships for the smallest, yet most abundant, stars in the Galaxy.

title: Star spots mimic the proposed abundance signatures of planet formation
comment: Submitted, comments welcome
summary: Trends with stellar elemental abundances and condensation temperature have been proposed as a possible tracer of rocky planet formation. Here we present an alternative explanation, where we show that stellar activity (star spots) can also cause apparent abundance changes in refractory elements preferentially over volatile elements. This effect arises naturally from atomic physics: refractory (rocky; high-$T_c$) elements preferentially have low first-ionization potentials, with strong transitions that are most sensitive to the cooler, magnetically-perturbed spot conditions, making any spot-induced change in line strength correlated with $T_c$. We re-examine literature on Sun-like stars in the Solar neighborhood and find that the $\log{R'_{HK}}$ stellar activity indicator is correlated with the so-called $T_c$ slope: the gradient of chemical abundances with respect to condensation temperature. Using 1D LTE Korg.jl simulations of the Sun with spots of varying size and contrast, we show that a wide range of spot configurations can manifest as abundance patterns that mimic a signal of abundance trends with condensation temperature. Finally, we conduct a line-by-line differential analysis of an ambient Solar spectrum relative to a Solar sunspot umbra to represent an extreme case, where we find that elements with high condensation temperature can show a factor of three (0.5 dex) increase. We discuss implications that stellar activity poses for precision spectroscopy, and provide some direction on how this effect might be mitigated.

AI.tldr: Stellar activity (star spots) can mimic the apparent correlation between stellar elemental abundances and condensation temperature that is often interpreted as a signature of rocky planet formation.
AI.motivation: Abundance trends with condensation temperature have been proposed as a tracer of rocky planet formation, but an alternative, non-planetary explanation needs to be tested.
AI.method: The authors re-examine literature on Sun-like stars in the Solar neighborhood, testing the correlation between the log R'_HK activity indicator and the Tc slope. They use 1D LTE Korg.jl simulations of the Sun with spots of varying size and contrast, and perform a line-by-line differential analysis of an ambient Solar spectrum relative to a Solar sunspot umbra.
AI.result: log R'_HK is correlated with the Tc slope. A wide range of spot configurations can reproduce abundance patterns mimicking a Tc trend, and in the extreme sunspot-umbra case, high-Tc elements can show a factor of three (0.5 dex) increase. This arises from atomic physics: refractory high-Tc elements preferentially have low first-ionization potentials and strong transitions sensitive to cooler, magnetically-perturbed spot conditions.
AI.conclusion: Stellar activity is a viable alternative explanation for observed abundance-condensation temperature trends, with implications for precision spectroscopy and possible mitigation strategies.

title: Anchoring the Chromospheric Activity$-$Rotation Relation: A Study of the Pleiades and Group X
comment: Accepted for publication in the AAS Journals
summary: We present a study of the rotation and the chromospheric H$α$ activity of low-mass stars in the $\approx$120 Myr-old Pleiades and the $\approx$400 Myr-old Group X open clusters. We combine published and new rotation periods ($P_\mathrm{rot}$) from TESS and ZTF, and use LAMOST, SDSS, and MDM spectra to measure H$α$ equivalent widths (EWs). While overall the Group X distributions of $P_\mathrm{rot}$ and EWs are as expected, detailed comparisons to the Pleiades and to the 700-Myr-old benchmark Praesepe produce some surprises. For F through mid K stars, the Group X color$-$period sequence lies between those of the Pleiades and of Praesepe, as expected. But the $P_\mathrm{rot}$ for its late K and early M dwarfs and the Praesepe slow-rotator sequence overlap, indicating that the 700 Myr-old stars have not spun down significantly despite being nearly twice as old as their Group X counterparts. In the Rossby number$-L_\mathrm{Hα}/L_\mathrm{bol}$ plane, rapid rotators in Group X are saturated, as is seen in older clusters, whereas the rapid rotators in the Pleiades show a weak but measurable dependence of $L_\mathrm{Hα}/L_\mathrm{bol}$ on rotation. This implies that the chromospheric activity$-$rotation relation attains its mature form between 120 and 400 Myr. Dividing the sample by color reveals that K, M0, and M1 dwarfs are no longer saturated by $\approx$120 Myr, M2 and M3 dwarfs become unsaturated between $\approx$400 and $\approx$700 Myr, and later M dwarfs remain largely saturated through field ages even as their saturated $L_\mathrm{Hα}/L_\mathrm{bol}$ levels decline, indicating that chromospheric evolution is not determined by rotation period alone.

AI.tldr: A comparative study of rotation periods and Hα activity in low-mass stars of the ~120 Myr Pleiades, the ~400 Myr Group X, and the 700 Myr Praesepe clusters reveals that the chromospheric activity–rotation relation reaches its mature form between 120–400 Myr, and that chromospheric evolution depends on more than rotation period alone.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to understand how rotation and chromospheric activity evolve in low-mass stars, using open clusters of different ages as benchmarks to test whether the activity–rotation relation and rotational spin-down follow a simple age sequence.
AI.method: Combined published and new rotation periods from TESS and ZTF with Hα equivalent widths from LAMOST, SDSS, and MDM spectra for low-mass stars in the Pleiades (~120 Myr), Group X (~400 Myr), and Praesepe (700 Myr); compared color–period sequences and positions in the Rossby number–L_Hα/L_bol plane.
AI.result: Group X color–period sequence lies between Pleiades and Praesepe for F through mid K stars as expected, but late K/early M Group X rotators overlap with the Praesepe slow-rotator sequence despite being half its age. Group X rapid rotators are saturated in the Rossby number–L_Hα/L_bol plane like older clusters, while Pleiades rapid rotators show a weak rotational dependence. Saturation ends at different ages depending on spectral type: K, M0, M1 by ~120 Myr; M2, M3 between ~400 and ~700 Myr; later M dwarfs remain largely saturated through field ages, with declining saturated L_Hα/L_bol levels.
AI.conclusion: Chromospheric activity–rotation relation attains its mature form between ~120 and ~400 Myr. Chromospheric evolution is not determined by rotation period alone, as saturation behavior depends strongly on spectral type and does not follow a simple age sequence.

title: Differential Luminosity Response of Balmer-Line Profiles in Galactic B/A Luminous Stars
comment: 15 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables
summary: We investigate the differential luminosity response of the optical Balmer series from H8 to H-alpha in Galactic B5-A5 luminous stars using homogeneous measurements of central depth, FWHM, and equivalent width at a resolving power of approximately 12,000. Direct line-to-line comparisons show a systematic change in the central-depth response toward the lower-order transitions. For the primary 72-star luminosity sample, the fitted luminosity coefficients show an overall positive trend with upper-level quantum number, with a point-estimate gradient of dq/dn = 0.0419. A joint Monte Carlo analysis with 10,000 realisations gives a median dq/dn = 0.0387 and a 95 percent interval from 0.0253 to 0.0532, with no non-positive gradients obtained. The higher-order H8-H-delta coefficients form a statistically unresolved plateau, followed by a well-supported increase in response magnitude from H-delta toward H-alpha. The result is robust to the adopted effective-temperature scale. The FWHM coefficients show no comparable Balmer-order progression, and the directly fitted profile-shape response is consistent with zero from H8 through H-beta. For H-alpha, the full logarithmic sample is not formally significant, whereas removal of the three remaining strongly filled-core profiles yields a significantly negative shape response. The observed behaviour is qualitatively compatible with the systematic variation of pressure broadening across the Balmer series, while the enhanced H-alpha response may additionally reflect non-LTE and wind-related effects.

AI.tldr: Homogeneous Balmer-series measurements in Galactic B5-A5 luminous stars reveal a systematic increase in luminosity response from higher- to lower-order transitions, peaking at H-alpha.
AI.motivation: Assess whether the luminosity sensitivity of optical Balmer lines varies systematically across the series, since Balmer lines are widely used as luminosity indicators and this Balmer-order dependence has not been characterized homogeneously.
AI.method: Central depth, FWHM, and equivalent width of H8 to H-alpha measured homogeneously at R ~ 12,000; line-to-line comparisons of fitted luminosity coefficients; Monte Carlo analysis with 10,000 realisations; robustness tests against the adopted effective-temperature scale; direct profile-shape fitting.
AI.result: Fitted central-depth luminosity coefficients rise with upper-level quantum number: point-estimate gradient dq/dn = 0.0419, Monte Carlo median 0.0387 (95 percent interval 0.0253-0.0532), with no non-positive gradients. H8-H-delta form a statistically unresolved plateau, followed by a well-supported increase toward H-alpha. FWHM coefficients show no Balmer-order progression, and profile-shape response is consistent with zero from H8 through H-beta; H-alpha shape response is formally insignificant for the full sample but significantly negative after removing three strongly filled-core profiles.
AI.conclusion: Balmer luminosity response is Balmer-order dependent, strengthening toward lower-order transitions and most pronounced at H-alpha; the trend is qualitatively consistent with systematic variation of pressure broadening across the series, with non-LTE and wind-related effects possibly enhancing H-alpha.
